ONE THING IS NOT SYMMETRIC, measured 2026-09-23. On the SERVER side the sequence reaches the C caller; on the CLIENT side it does not. Neither `rclc_client_take_response(client, data, capacity, *len)` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/rclc/detail/nros_generated.h:7768`) nor `nros_client_take_response_raw(client, buf, buf_len)` (`:7668`) returns one, although the vtable slot beneath them does (`packages/core/nros-rmw-abi/include/nros/rmw_vtable.h:374-388` — `*seq_out` is the id of the request the reply answers, issue 0778's other half). It is dropped on purpose: a nano-ros client keeps ONE call in flight, so there is nothing to correlate a reply against. See `cpp:Client::prune_pending_requests` for that model and `rust:RequestId` for the divergence that would change it.
